translation:
...continued from the meaning of the previous verse... "the desired enjoyments they themselves have created." ||22||

Meaning: But the fruit gained by those of little intelligence is perishable — those who worship the gods attain the gods, but My devotees attain Me. Whoever worships a particular deity becomes that deity's vehicle (vahana); regarding this it is said:

_Yasya devasya yadrupam tatha bhushanavahanam, tadrupa eva tacchaktir asuran yoddhum abhyayau. ||21||_
(Whatever form, ornaments, and vehicle belong to a given deity, that same deity's own power (shakti) arose in that very form to do battle with the demons.)

Swami Vivekanandaji has said in one place:

The various forms of worship of the gods (devatas) are all part of ritualistic religion (karmakand). Through them the worshipper certainly gets help in obtaining various kinds of divine enjoyments, but through them neither devotion (bhakti) nor liberation (mukti) can be attained. For this reason the Vedas have condemned worshippers of other deities, calling them ignorant; in some places they are even called animals:

_Atha yo'nyam devatam upaste anyo'sav anyo'ham asmiti na sa veda yatha pashuh._
(He who worships another deity, thinking "he is one and I am another," does not know the truth — he is like an animal.)

And in the Gita they are called of little intelligence.

One who takes shelter under the shade of a mere form (akar) — if instead he takes shelter under Parbrahm, he can be saved; regarding this it is said:

_Koi koi jogi bach gaye, Parbrahmaki ot,
Chakki chalti kaalki, padi sabhi par chot. ||63||_
(Some yogis, and only some, escaped by taking shelter in Parbrahm; the mill of Time keeps turning, and its blow falls on everyone else.)

Meaning: Those few yogis who took shelter in Parbrahm Parmatma were saved from the fear of Time (Kaal); everyone else has been struck by the ever-turning mill of Time. Kabirji says that other deities keep us away from devotion to Vishnu, keeping us apart from God.

_Kabir mai mashani shethi, Shitala Bheru bhoot Hanumant,
Sahebsu nyara rahai, jo inko poojant. ||64||_
(Kabir says: the Mother goddesses, the cremation-ground attendant-deities, Shitala, Bhairav, ghosts, Hanuman — whoever worships these remains separated from the Lord.)

Meaning: If one worships and serves the Mother goddesses, the cremation-ground attendant-deities, Shitala, Bhairav, ghosts, Hanuman, and other tamasic deities and demigods, they keep him away from devotion to God.

For this reason, creation is of two kinds: one is the mental creation (mansi srishti), the other is the sexual/procreative creation (maithuni srishti).

_Omkarse upno, Jivan jug sansar,
Rarankarse upno, so Sadguruko parivar. ||47||_
(From Omkar arose, O Jivan, the age-bound world; from Rarankar arose the true Guru's own family.)

_Omkarmaan aatle, sur Brahma munidev,
Rarankarmaan Jivana, je laga Sadguru sev. ||48||_
(Within Omkar wander, caught, the gods, Brahma, and sage-deities; within Rarankar, O Jivan, are those who have taken to the true Guru's service.)

_Akshar akshar ek Jivana, Omkarki aad,
Mamase raro bado, so Sadguru kahyo vichar. ||49||_
(Of all the letters, O Jivan, Om is the foremost; but "Ra" is greater than "Ma" — this is the teaching the true Guru has declared.)

_Ek aksharthi Jivana, bhayo brahmand vistar,
Raro rakhyo Harijana, mamo bhayo sansar. ||50||_
(From a single letter, O Jivan, the vast universe expanded; "Ra" is reserved for God's own people, "Ma" became the world.)

_E khare pade nahi Jivana, akal avinashi roop,
So gau charave Nandki, je Dashrath kul badbhoop. ||51||_
(This, O Jivan, never perishes — it is the imperishable, incomprehensible form; that same one grazes Nanda's cows, and is the great king of Dashrath's lineage.)

_Khare pade nahi Jivana, adbad ek aroop,
Utpat pralo jahaan jai same, so Sitapatiko roop. ||52||_
(It never perishes, O Jivan — it is one wondrous, formless being; where creation and dissolution both merge and rest, that is the form of Sitapati, the Lord of Sita.)

Jivanji Maharaj says that from the Omkar Pranav mantra arose the living creation under the sway of Maya — the mass of beings caught in the cycle of birth and death. But separate from this world born of Omkar, from the sound of Rarankar arose, free from the three gunas and desire-bound action, the true Guru's family — in the form of a reflection of Parbrahm — that is, the individual souls (jivatmas) who recognize Parbrahm. ||47||

_Rarankarku kahat hai, Brahma sarupi Ram,
Santdas tihu lokmein, sabahi iska kaam. ||65||_
(Rarankar, it is said, is Ram, of the very form of Brahm; O Santdas, in all three worlds, everything is His doing.)

"Ram," who is Parbrahm in form and beyond even Brahm, and by whose direction the activity of all three worlds proceeds — by His will alone all beings act. Here, under His shelter, the members of the true Guru's family, the disciples, have arisen from Rarankar, and it is into Him alone that they are to merge.

Within Omkar, which governs creation, sustenance, and dissolution, pundits, Brahma, sages, and gods keep colliding and wandering, being swept again and again through the stream of birth and death in this universe. But those who, remaining in the shelter of the true Guru, practise devotion and worship without desire — their place is established at the feet of Shri Ram, who is Parbrahm in form. ||48||

Jivanji Maharaj says that those who take refuge in Omkar have been deluded. This is because, among the words of the alphabet used to address the Lord Parbrahm, both the word "Om" and the letter "Ra" of the word "Ram" (which is Parbrahm's own form) occur. Because the word Om grants worldly action, karma, and its fruits, ordinary people of dull understanding are drawn more strongly toward it; and since the word Om has an attractive, decorative quality, the soul is pulled toward it the way a moth is pulled toward a flame. The letter "Ra," on the other hand, is not a word that has been specially embellished or falsely publicized in order to bring about attainment of the pure form of Parbrahm — it remains confined to true devotees alone. Thus, more than "A-U-M," the letter "Ra" in the word "Ram" is the finest and best of the entire alphabet, because by the utterance of its sound one attains Parbrahm. This is what the true Guru, having understood it, has declared. ||49||

From the single word of the imperishable, spotless, formless Parbrahm — who never perishes — this creation was formed, like an egg (anda). Among all beings in this universe, devotees who know this secret and are resolved to remain ever absorbed in devotion to Narayan have accepted and adopted the chanting of Rarankar as their constant remembrance. All other beings besides these devotees of God (Harijans) have accepted the word "Om," which ends in the letter "Ma," and so have fallen into the cycle of birth and death. ||50||

Jivanji Maharaj says that the name of Parbrahm is imperishable (akshaya) — that is, it does not decay or perish; moreover it is unaging and immortal, it does not fall or fade, meaning it does not perish; it is indestructible and incomprehensible. This same form of Parbrahm grazes King Nanda's cows in Gokul, and is the great King of Vraj who illumines the lineage of Dashrath. ||51||

He continues further, saying that the account of this imperishable, immortal form is wondrous — one of dull understanding cannot grasp it. Moreover, it is the form of Sitapati, the Lord of Sita, in whom creation and dissolution both merge, and He alone is Parbrahm. ||52||

With Rarankar in view, Rohidas composed this hymn (pad) in the Godi raga:

Godi:

_Jab ham Ram Ram, kahi gavega,
Rarankar hai tahai soi, taso antarmai milavega. ||Teka||
Loha samdrashta kanchan samdrashta, vish amrit sang dhavega,
Surnar muni durlabh pad, sohi tere avega. ||1||
Guru parsad bhai anbhe mat, bhed abhed milavega,
Kahe Rohidas meri aapa par, tab wa thade pavega. ||2||_
(When we sing "Ram, Ram," that very Rarankar dwelling within will unite our heart with Himself; iron and gold will seem the same to us, and worldly poison will run instead toward nectar; the state hard even for gods, men, and sages to attain will come to you. By the Guru's grace the mind becomes fearless, and the distinction between "different" and "non-different" dissolves; Rohidas says, when I stand beyond my own self, then He will be found standing right before me.)

Meaning: Rohidasji says that when we perform bhajan by chanting "Ram, Ram," that name of Ram will unite our inner self with God, who dwells there in the form of Rarankar. Then, whether it be iron or gold, we shall look upon both with equal vision (samdrishti), and even the poison-like objects of this world will begin to run toward the nectar-essence of Ram. Moreover, that state which is hard to attain even for gods, men, and sages will come to us. By the Guru's grace our mind will become fearless, and it will bring about union with the manifest form of God who lies hidden, concealed within this triple-natured (trigunī) creation. Rohidas says that when such ego (ahankar) is thus removed from within us, we shall find the essence of God standing directly before us.

It is said in the Samagam that taking shelter under a mere form does not save one who himself has form — meaning that whoever takes refuge in a god or goddess can receive only as much protection as that deity's own power allows. Therefore, of the creation that God has made in this world, it is fashioned in two ways: the first is the mental creation (mansi srishti), and the second is the sexual/procreative creation (maithuni srishti). The learned have also stated it as two kinds: the first, the creation of living beings (jiva srishti), and the second, the creation of the Lord (Ishwar srishti) — thus two kinds of creation have been described.

According to the principles of the Nyaya school regarding the soul (atma), fourteen qualities are attributed to the soul in its embodied (jiva) form: (1) pleasure, (2) pain, (3) ignorance, (4) desire, (5) aversion, (6) effort, (7) righteousness (dharma), (8) unrighteousness (adharma), (9) latent impressions of knowledge (sanskara), (10) number, (11) modification, (12) distinctness, (13) conjunction, and (14) disjunction.

It is said that God has manifested four kinds of creation:
1. The divine or godly creation (daivi, or sursampatti).
2. The demonic creation, or the creation of the flow (asuri srishti, or pravah srishti) — in the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that there are only two kinds of creation; of these, the first is called the divine creation, and it has two further divisions, giving:
3. Maryada srishti — manifested by Brahma through the mind, in which beings such as Sanaka and his brothers, and Narada, appeared.
4. Pushti srishti — created from God's own limb, this is the creation that depends upon the path of Krishna's grace (kripanugraha). Whoever takes refuge in whichever kind of creation (form) has safety only for as long as that creation exists. The Gita, chapter 9, says:

_Te tam bhuktva swargalokam vishalam, kshine punye martyalokam vishanti,
Evam trayidharmam anuprapanna gatagatam kaamkaama labhante. ||21||_
(Having enjoyed that vast heaven, when their merit is exhausted, they attain the world of mortals; thus those who take shelter in the desire-driven path of Vedic religion, and who desire sense objects, undergo repeated coming and going.)

Activity proceeds within these two kinds of creation, that of Omkar and that of Rarankar. Within Omkar falls the creation bound by the three gunas, while Rarankar is a fourth state that transcends the three gunas. This devotion to Rarankar is practised only by the true followers of the true Guru; the Vedas and Puranas, on the other hand, proceed in accordance with the principle of Omkar. Therefore Jivanji Maharaj says:

_Pothi Parbrahm naamki, Sadgurue diya bataay,
Aadya avinashi Jivana, Ra re Ma me chit laay. ||66|| (Gurudev)_
(The true Guru has revealed the scripture of Parbrahm's name; O Jivan, fix your mind on the primordial, imperishable — on "Ra" and "Ma.")

Meaning: The four Vedas, the six Shastras, the eighteen Puranas, and many other such texts and scriptures exist, but the true Guru has revealed the scripture — the secret key — that shows genuine devotion in the shortest possible form, in which the mystery of the Supreme Truth is contained: the name of God. In this name dwells the primordial and imperishable Supreme Being, resting on only two letters, "Ra" and "Ma." Keep your attention fixed only on this name of Ram.

_Kabir padhvo dur kar, aru pustak de bahaay,
Pachaas akshar parhari, tu Ra re Ma me chit laay. ||67|| (Sar ka Ang)_
(Kabir says: give up studying, and cast away your books; abandon fifty letters, and fix your mind on "Ra" and "Ma.")

Meaning: Give up reading and studying scriptures and texts, set aside those books, and abandon fifty of the fifty-two letters as well; fix your attention on devotion and remembrance of God using only the two letters "Ra" and "Ma" within the name Ram.

Jivanji Maharaj goes even further than this.

_Bavan aksharmaan Jivana, ek akshar tatvasaar,
Ma maa pahelo je likhyo, teno Ved na pave paar. ||68|| (Prabodh)_
(Among the fifty-two letters, O Jivan, one letter is the essence of the truth: the one written before "Ma" — even the Vedas cannot fathom it.)

Meaning: Among the fifty-two letters of the alphabet, only one letter is especially important, and that is the letter in the name Ram which comes before "Ma" — that is, "Ra." Even the Vedas cannot fathom its mystery.

Kabirji says:

_Kabir akshar bolte, Omkar anusaar,
Aakarke bekaarko, moodh kahe Kirtaar. ||69||_
(Kabir says: one who merely utters the syllable in accordance with Omkar — the useless thing bound to mere form — the fool calls that the Creator.)

Meaning: One who follows and worships Omkar keeps repeating the syllable "Om, Om," but foolish, dull-witted people call this useless, three-gunas-bound Omkar the Supreme Being itself.

Here, Jivanji Maharaj has thus set forth the true form of Parbrahm. He has also shown Parbrahm as the Lord of the entire universe, and as the Lord of the devotees of Shri Hari's own dear ones (nija jan). Further, he has shown the division and multiplication of the gunas. At this point, a doubt arises on the opposing side (purvapaksha): if the universe worships "Omkar," why does Jivanji Maharaj speak of "Rarankar"? Let us first understand the matter of Omkar.

_Om ityetad aksharam idam sarvam, tasyopavyakhyanam bhutam bhavad bhavishyad iti sarvam omkara eva, yad anyat trikalatitam tad api omkara eva. ||23|| (Mandukya 1-1-1)_
(The syllable Om alone is everything; it is the explanation of whatever was, is, and will be. Therefore, whatever exists is Omkar alone; and whatever else exists beyond the three times — past, present, future — that too is Omkar alone.)

_Esha sarveshvara esha sarvajnah, esho'ntaryamy esha yonih sarvasya, prabhavapyayau hi bhutanam. ||24|| (Mandukya 1-1-6)_
(He is the Lord of all, He is omniscient, He is the indweller, and because He is the source of the origin and dissolution of all beings, He alone is the cause of everything.)

Furthermore, the Taittiriya Upanishad says:

_Om iti Brahma, Om itidam sarvam, Om ityetad anukritir hasma vaa apyashravayantyashravayanti, Om iti samani gayanti, Om shom iti shastrani shamsanti, Om ityadhvaryuh pratigaram pratigrinati, Om iti Brahma prasauti, Om ityagnihotram anujanati, Om iti Brahmanah pravakshyannaha brahmopapnavaniti. (Tai. 1-8-1)_
(The word Om is Brahman, for Om is all forms; Om is repetition. Saying "O Shravaya," one is made to listen with Om. Saying Om, the Sama hymns are sung — the chanting of the Samaveda. Saying Om, the sacred verses are recited. The adhvaryu priest utters Om after every ritual act. Saying Om, Brahma, the presiding deity of the Atharvaveda, grants permission. Saying Om, Agni consents to the performance of the sacrifice. Saying Om, a Brahmin who has not studied the Vedas nevertheless begins with Om. Saying Om, one expresses the wish, "May I attain Parbrahm.")

Resolution (Samadhan): We accept that all beings begin their worldly activity by first uttering the word "Om." And we have already said that the creation which arose from Omkar belongs to the path of desire-bound action (sakam karma). Those who perform the Vedic rites of yajna and sacrifice do so hoping for the fruit of their actions; and desire-bound action can never be without purpose — behind every action lies a definite result, and the soul must experience the good or bad fruit gained from that action. Furthermore, when the scripture (shruti) says that Om is omniscient and is the form of Parbrahm, that is not correct, because those who know only Omkar have stopped right there — they have not been able to go further, nor have they gained the capacity to understand the creation that lies beyond it. Their understanding is therefore like that of a frog in a well. Those who remain absorbed and content within the creation of Omkar experience only creation and dissolution — for they will never emerge from the whirlpool of birth and death, again and again. Regarding such souls, Kabirji says:

_Jhoothe sukhku sukh kahe, kachhu manat hai man mod,
E jagat chaveno kalko, kachhu mukhmein kachhu god. ||70||_
(He calls false happiness true happiness, and his mind takes some delight in it; this world is Time's own deceit — something in the mouth, something else hidden in the lap.)

This is because the fruit of action obtained through the worship of Omkar and the like, and the happiness gained by it, are merely a fleeting rush of feeling — not true happiness. Therefore Kabirji, giving a warning, says:

_Omkar nishre bhaya, so karta mati jaan,
Saacha shabd Kabirka, parde maanhi pichhaan. ||71|| (Sumiran-24)_
(Do not take the settled Omkar to be the Doer; recognize Kabir's true word hidden within the veil.)

To one who, by sounding the word Om, feels a certain sense of happiness, Kabirji says this is not the truth, so do not be misled by it. Kabirji has shown the true word. Do not take the settled, fixed Omkar to be the true Doer; instead, understand and reflect upon Ram, who dwells hidden within the body — behind the veil — the body made of the five elements. For —

_Jivroopyak antarbaasa, antarjyotiki naa pargaasa. ||2||_
(The soul dwells within, one in the form of the individual jiva; the inner light does not become manifest.)

We have already said that the individual soul (jiva), in the form of the collective (samashti), has taken up residence within the body; its awareness (surata) is something distinct. Though dwelling in this world, it remains untouched by it. What is called the "inner light" (antar jyoti) is the light of Parbrahm's own realm, which, by awakening awareness within the conscious soul, gives rise to the mind and its impressions (sanskaras), and thereby the soul becomes worldly, entangled in this world. If, in this state, one forgets Parbrahm, there remains the danger of turning onto the path of untruth. If the soul remains caught in delusion, it goes astray and misses the experience of the inner light. Today, because of external attractions in the world, the words of the true Guru cannot be understood, and so the soul loses its way. When the essence of the soul mistakes external light for Brahman, it falls into delusion. Therefore it must seek out the true path. If the meaning of the name "Ram," as explained by the true Guru, is neither known nor understood, then the soul, taking merely a worldly meaning, turns from its collective (samashti) form into an individual (vyashti) form. And this very process today, of turning from the collective form into the individual form, is itself the illusion (maya) in the form of the Gayatri. Just as the pure soul, by considering itself Brahman, has become impure — some regard it as the cause of the world, others regard it as the material cause — yet that so-called pure form of Brahman, even while called pure, is not pure; it is impure, that is, false (mithya). This is because those who belong to God (bhagwatjan) are free from all desires and from the world, as we have already established earlier. Whereas Omkar is bound by desire; the shruti (scripture) says:

_Tadetanmithunamomityaitasminnakshare sansrijyate yada vai,
Mithunau samagachchhata aapayata vai tavanyobhyasya kaamam. ||25||_
(This union is joined together by the syllable "Om." At the time when the pair come together, each obtains fulfilment of the other's desires — that is, "Om" is thereby proven to possess the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires.)

Furthermore, the original teacher of the world, Shankaracharya, says:

_Yatha loke mithunau mithunavayavau stri punsau yada samagachchhato... gunvatvam omkarasya siddham ityabhiprayah... (Cha. 1-1-6)_
(Just as in the world a pair — a man and a woman as the members of the pair — come together, uniting through the ordinary act, and at that time fulfil each other's desires, so likewise, through this indwelling union, it is established that Omkar possesses the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires.)

Here, commenting on the Chandogya Upanishad, it is stated that just as in the world a pair (mithuna) — that is, a man and a woman as the members of the pair — come together, uniting through the ordinary act of intercourse, and at that time fulfil each other's desires, in the same manner, through this indwelling union, it is established that Omkar possesses the quality of granting the fulfilment of all desires. This is our view.

Further, it is stated in a later section that the wise one (meaning the worshipper) who worships the syllable of the Udgitha word (the syllable chanted by the priest called Udgata) becomes one who brings about the fulfilment of all desires.

That is, such a Brahmin becomes capable of fulfilling even the complete desires of his patron (yajman) — that is, that Brahmin himself becomes subject to karma; and moreover, the patron for whom the mantras and rites are performed also, without fail, becomes bound to enjoy the fruits of that karma. It is further stated there that —

_Taddha etadanusaaksharam yadi kim chatujanatyo mityeva tadaha esha eva samriddhir yadanujna, samdharyata ha vai kamanam bhavati ya etadevam vidwan aksharam udgitham upaste. ||8||_
(Om itself is the syllable of consent; whenever anyone grants permission for anything, he says "Om." This granting of consent is itself abundance. If a person who knows this in this way worships the syllable Udgitha, he attains abundance of desires — he certainly attains the complete abundance of all his desires.)

For this very reason Jivanji Maharaj said to Krishnadas —

_Jot swaroop teenku thaharaya, Aadya Purush kinahu nahi paya,
Khat darshan tabhi upaye, Omkarku sabahi dhyaye. ||72||_
(They have taken the form of light to be the ultimate three; none has attained the Primordial Being; the six schools of philosophy arose only then, and all of them meditate upon Omkar.)

Thus, by declaring Omkar itself to be the form of divine light, the whole world has fallen into delusion, and cannot understand who the Primordial Being (Adya Purush) truly is; instead, people become absorbed in the worship of other deities, so that their lives are wasted in vain. Moreover, the fear of birth and death does not leave them — it does not spare even the gods. The deities whom human beings worship, considering them immortal, are themselves not immortal; when their merit (punya karma) is exhausted, they too must take birth again, and they too live in fear of death, because —

_Tanu tatra mrityuryatha matsyamudake paripashyedevam paryapashyadayi saamni yajushi,
Te nu viditvordhwa richah saamno yajushah swaram eva pravishan. ||26||_
("Just as a fisherman spots fish in the water, in the same way Death spotted these deities engaged in the rites connected with the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas. Having come to know this, the deities withdrew from the rites connected with the Rig, Sama, and Yajur, and entered into pure sound.")

That is, just as fish become trapped in a fisherman's net and meet death, in the same way all beings — gods, gandharvas, kinnaras, human beings, and others of the maithuni (procreative) creation — become caught in death because of the fruits of their actions; that is, the fear of birth, old age, and death remains with them constantly. Here the question arises: where did Death see the deities? Death (Kaal) saw that once their karma was exhausted, the deities would come under his control — that is, once their merit is used up, they must take birth again in some other womb. Realizing this, the deities understood that their ritual works (karmakand) could no longer sustain them, and they became afraid. We have already said earlier that the gods enjoy their prosperity through the fruits of the offerings (homa) given to them by human beings, and that they are prepared to do anything to preserve that prosperity. Thus, even while understanding the truth, they are unable to follow it, for the sake of such fleeting happiness. Therefore the true Guru has told us —

_Tab to Omkar hi bhayo, Mayako sarno teen grahyo,
Omkar tab srishti nipaai, taki khabar kinahu nahi paai,
Aadya Purush te bhoole tabahi, Omkarku bhaage sabahi._
(Then it was Omkar alone that came to be, taking shelter under the three modes of Maya; Omkar then brought forth creation, but none has ever grasped its true nature; forgetting the Primordial Being at that very point, everyone has run after Omkar.)

Thus, falling under the delusion of momentary greed, the world has clung to Omkar and has forgotten the true Parbrahm. Like a blind man falling into a well, the world has fallen straight into the mouth of Death. All its cherished desires remain unfulfilled. Those who walk the path of the six schools of philosophy (khat darshan) do not realize that they are walking, of their own accord, straight into the mouth of Death — this is exactly like walking of one's own will straight into the mouth of a tiger. For this reason it is said in the Mahabharata —

_Chaturnam lokapalanam shukrasyatha brihaspateh,
Marutam vishwadevanam sadhyanamashwirapi. ||27||
Rudradityavasunam cha tathanyesham divaukasam,
Ete vai nirayastaat sthanasya paramatmanah. ||28|| (Shanti-198-5,6)_
(Varuna, Kubera, Indra, and Yamaraja — these four guardians of the world — and Shukra, Brihaspati, the Marut gods, the Vishvadevas, the Sadhyas, the Ashwini Kumaras, Rudra, the Adityas, the Vasus, and other deities — the abodes of all of these are, in comparison with the Supreme Abode of the Paramatma, like hell.)

For this very reason Jivanji Maharaj has said —

_Jahaan jahaan pandit paav dhare, tahaan tahaan Jamka vaas,
Sant paanv dhare Jivana, tahaan Sitapati avinash. ||73||_
(Wherever the pandit sets foot, there dwells Yama; wherever the saint sets foot, O Jivan, there is the imperishable Sitapati.)

That is, as long as the covering of Maya (illusion) that clings to the soul is not removed and its delusion is not destroyed, the soul cannot recognize Parbrahm. But as soon as the delusion is destroyed, it begins to experience Parbrahm directly. Regarding this, Kabirji says —

_Kabir gunakaar gun vistaryo, jab dhariyu e deh,
Bhagakaar tabe padhyo, sarvaale sahaj videh. ||53||_
(Kabir says: the gunas expanded through multiplication when this body was assumed; then division was learned; and in the sum total, effortlessly, one becomes bodiless.)

Kabirji has composed this couplet (sakhi) by bringing together the idea of division and multiplication. That is, our true Guru has performed a division of actions (karmas) and gunas — meaning Kabirji says that the gunas and karmas must be divided down, that they must gradually be reduced to zero. This is the state the soul must reach, where no number remains left over. It is for this reason that zero has been called the complete number — for when it is attained, all craving dissolves, and supreme bliss is attained, before which every worldly happiness appears puny.

In the end, whoever walks by relying upon the Guru's word incurs no karma, and no bondage remains for him. Thus, by the support of a single word, he can cross the ocean of worldly existence. This is the very matter being explained here: whoever wishes to take refuge in Shri Hari must give up all manner of crooked reasoning and argument, and hold fast to the path of good virtue (sadgun), so that, without wandering here and there elsewhere in the world, he may go straight to the Supreme Abode, into the refuge of Shri Hari.

Explaining the sense of this couplet, the revered Yadunath Maharaj has written: just as multiplication increases a number and division decreases it, so too the three gunas, when expanded, became the twenty-five categories (prakritis) of the five elements; and when the prakritis are drawn back in, only the five remain as five, and finally only the ego (aham) remains — and when that too is destroyed, only Ishwar remains alone.

When a body is assumed, the three gunas multiply together with the five elements, and so karma increases; but when the three-guna number belonging to Omkar is divided by Rarankar, the state of zero — the bodiless (videh) form — is attained easily and naturally, in a simple manner. Here, the "sum" of karma means, in the end — that is, at the conclusion of the process of multiplication, division, subtraction, and so on — the final outcome of karma. "Sum equals bodiless" means that at the end of the process of multiplication and division, the one who takes refuge in the true Guru attains the bodiless, effortless, zero-state of Parbrahm.

Narsinh Mehta was a devotee wholly devoted to Krishna alone. This was displeasing to the sannyasis (renunciate ascetics), and so seventeen sannyasis lodged a complaint against Narsinh Mehta before Ra' Mandalik, the king of the old monastery, saying that Narsinh Mehta was a hypocrite. They therefore had a garland placed upon the image of Damodardasji, saying that if God Himself gave that garland to Narsinh, only then would his devotion be judged true — otherwise he should be sentenced to death. At that time Narsinh Mehta sang the bhajans of the Harmala (garland cycle), in which he sharply rebuked the sannyasis and strongly criticized Omkar.

Raag Maru:

_Siddhi na hoy re Shripatne, siddhi na hoy re,
Vaishnav vina taryo na koy re. ||Tek||
Kahoji kayo sannyasi sharan ja paamyo, dandvesh jataadhari re,
Tamo Vaishnavoni ninda karo chho, bhoonda narakna adhikari re. ||1||
Tamari stri mare ne jyare khava tale, tyare bhagvaan pahero re,
Preet bhagati vairaag vina, fooko kaan ja beharo re. ||2||
Tamara Omkarnu karo re athanu, mahara Vrindavan chalo re,
Bhaje Narsaiyo mahelo dand kamandal, maahari poodhe taal vagado re. ||3||_
(Shripat shall never attain perfection — none has ever crossed over without being a Vaishnav. Tell me, which sannyasi, wearing the staff and matted locks, has ever attained true refuge? You slander the Vaishnavs, and so you deserve a wretched hell. When your wife dies and you have nothing to eat, only then do you put on the ochre robe; without true love, devotion, and renunciation, you merely blow into a deaf man's ear. Go pickle your Omkar — come instead to my Vrindavan! Narsaiya sings: give up your staff and water-pot, and play the cymbals with me instead.)

Meaning: Ascetics such as those called Shripat will never succeed in crossing the ocean of worldly existence, because no one can cross it without being a Vaishnav. Tell me yourselves — has anyone, merely by holding a staff and taking on the garb of a sannyasi or matted locks, ever managed to reach the refuge of God? You yourselves slander the Vaishnavs — you are so wicked that you deserve to attain a wretched hell. When your wife dies and, at that time of unease in the funeral rites, you feel restless, you put on ochre robes and become sannyasis; but without true love and renunciation for God, you merely make the sound of Omkar, blowing into the conch that produces the Omkar sound, blowing the mantra of Omkar into the ears of the deaf — that is, the uncomprehending. You urge people to practise the worship of Omkar, but such a useless Omkar, good for nothing, you may as well go on hoarding uselessly. If you truly wish your own good, give up ritualism (karmakand) and join me instead in devotion to Krishna of Vrindavan, and play the cymbals (kansi-manjira) while singing bhajans and kirtans.

Thus, in devotion to Vishnu (Vaishnav bhakti), devotees such as Narsinh Mehta have condemned Omkar as being like a thief posing as an honest merchant.
